title: Installment Amounts on the Self-Pay Visit Package: Scheduled Share and Amount Collected
content:
**Billing office memo — Self-Pay Visit Package installments.** The amount collected for a past-due installment is defined from the package's own record and its payment history as follows.

**1. Installments already paid.** These are the installment payments recorded in the package history; both their number and their total in dollars are read from that history.

**2. Due date of the next unpaid installment.** The due date of the next unpaid installment is the purchase date plus the tier's installment interval in calendar days for every installment already paid.

**3. The last installment.** The installment being collected is the last one when the installments already paid, counted together with it, reach the number of installments the package's price is paid in, as recorded on the package.

**4. Scheduled share.** The scheduled share of an installment that is not the last is the purchase price divided by the number of installments, rounded to the cent; the scheduled share of the last installment is the purchase price less every installment payment already received.

**5. Amount collected.** A past-due installment is collected at its scheduled share. The amount collected is stated to the cent and is never below $0.00.

**Worked figures (hypothetical package records)**

| Purchase price | Installments | Already paid | Installment collected | Last? | Scheduled share and amount collected |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $1000.00 | 3 | none | 1st | No | $1000.00 divided by 3, rounded: $333.33 |
| $1000.00 | 3 | $333.33 | 2nd | No | $333.33 |
| $1000.00 | 3 | $333.33 and $333.33 | 3rd | Yes | $1000.00 less $666.66: $333.34 |
| $1236.00 | 2 | $618.00 | 2nd | Yes | $1236.00 less $618.00: $618.00 |

**Due dates on the same hypothetical package** (purchase date as day 0, an interval of 30 calendar days): with no installment paid the next unpaid installment is due on day 0; with one paid, on day 30; with two paid, on day 60.
